name: Polar sea ice
summary: Arctic sea ice 1.53M km² and Antarctic 1.46M km² below average on 7 Nov
state: On 7 Nov Arctic sea-ice extent was 8.55 million km², about 1.53 million below the 1981–2010 average and fifth-lowest for the date. Antarctic extent was 15.46 million km², about 1.46 million below average and third-lowest for the date (NSIDC). Both are past the −1.0 million Watch line, and neither pole is at a record low for the date.
for_you: Sea-ice loss mainly affects polar ecosystems, regional climate and shipping routes. It has no immediate effect on most people's daily lives.
rubric_hit: Watch: Arctic -1.53M km² and Antarctic -1.46M km² both below -1.0M line; no record low for the date (7 Nov)
why: Sea ice reflects sunlight and regulates ocean circulation; record lows accelerate warming.
drivers: Air and ocean temperatures, winds, season.

rubric.alert: Either pole at a record low for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Arctic and Antarctic extent anomalies both above −1.0 million km² vs 1981–2010.
